indications: cough (catarrhs and defluxions of thin rheums causing a continual cough)
242:Poppy.ancient_dosage: distilled water of the flowers drank evening and morning
242:Poppy.source_quote: The garden Poppy heads with seeds made into a syrup, is frequently, and to good effect used to procure rest, and sleep, in the sick and weak

indications: absent or delayed menstruation (to bring down women's courses)
cough (cough and stuffing of the chest by colds)
depression (melancholy and heaviness, or sadness of spirits)
headache (pains in the head coming of a cold cause)
vertigo (running or swimming in the head)
preparations: fumigation (sitting over the hot fumes of the decoction)
120:Feverfew.ancient_dosage: a decoction of the flowers in wine, with a little Nutmeg or Mace, drank often in a day
120:Feverfew.source_quote: It is very effectual for all pains in the head coming of a cold cause, the herb being bruised and applied to the crown of the head

indications: urinary retention (opens the passages of the urine)
urinary tract abscesses and ulcers (imposthumes and inward ulcers in the urinary passage)
sleeplessness during fever (to procure rest and sleep to bodies distempered by the heat of ague fits)
preparations: cooked as a pot-herb in broth
100:Dandelion.source_quote: It is of an opening and cleansing quality, and therefore very effectual for the obstructions of the liver, gall and spleen, and the diseases that arise from them, as the jaundice and hypocondriac

indications: internal injuries and bruises (inward hurts, bruises)
catarrh (defluction of rheum from the head upon the lungs)
diarrhea and dysentery (fluxes of blood or humours by the belly)
breast engorgement (breasts that grow sore by the abundance of milk)
preparations: poultice (fresh root beaten and spread on leather)
86:Comfrey.source_quote: The Great Comfrey helps those that spit blood, or make a bloody urine.

indications: chest and lung complaints (griefs of the breast and lungs)
painful urination (the stranguary, heat of urine)
preparations: linctus (juice in Rose-water with Gum Tragacanth)
180:Liquorice.source_quote: Liquorice boiled in fair water, with some Maiden-hair and figs, makes a good drink for those that have a dry cough or hoarseness, wheezing or shortness of breath

indications: rabid dog bites (bitings of mad dogs)
abdominal cramps (griping pains of the belly)
cysts and hard swellings (wens, kernels, or hard swelling)
